text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.71% today, closing out a tough two-week stretch down 10%. The stock moved lower on the same day the company reported its quarterly earnings and announced a leadership change, suggesting investors reacted negatively to either the financial results themselves or what management signaled about the road ahead. Oil prices remain elevated—U.S. crude at $103 a barrel—but refineries are running near full capacity at 92.8%, which limits upside for refining margins.

The broader context matters too: refiners have faced headwinds despite strong crude prices because profit margins depend on the gap between what they pay for oil and what they charge for finished fuel, and that spread has tightened as gasoline and diesel stockpiles have built up. Political risk also emerged on the same day—news about the midterms raised the possibility of a Democratic Congress pushing more renewable energy, which could weigh on long-term sentiment in fossil fuel refining stocks.
